findings.issue_text: [P1, confidence 100] src/sentry/spans/buffer.py:197 — `p.zadd(set_key, {span.payload: span.end_timestamp_precise for span in subsegment})` — This changes live `span-buf:s:*` keys from Redis sets to sorted sets without a versioned keyspace or migration, so every pre-deploy buffered segment makes the new writer fail with WRONGTYPE and stops span ingestion until that key expires.

[P2, confidence 100] src/sentry/scripts/spans/add-buffer.lua:30 — `for i = 0, 1000 do` — A trace whose redirect chain exceeds 1,001 links stops resolution at an intermediate span instead of the segment root, splitting one trace across independently flushed segments after this change reduced the previously documented 10,000-link bound.

[P1, confidence 100] src/sentry/api/paginator.py:838 — `return int(math.floor(value) if self._is_asc(for_prev) else math.ceil(value))` — The new paginator is wired to audit-log `order_by="-datetime"` but treats each `AuditLogEntry.datetime` as a numeric value, so an authorized request with `optimized_pagination=true` crashes while building the cursor instead of returning audit logs.

[P2, confidence 75] src/sentry/scripts/spans/add-buffer.lua:47 — `span_count = redis.call("zunionstore", set_key, 2, set_key, span_key)` — The default ZUNIONSTORE SUM aggregation doubles the score of an identical payload present in both merged buffers, so eviction ranks that duplicate as newer than its real end timestamp and removes a newer distinct span when the segment crosses 1,000 members.

[P1, confidence 100] src/sentry/scripts/spans/add-buffer.lua:63 — `redis.call("zpopmin", set_key, span_count - 1000)` has no test that creates more than 1,000 timestamp-distinct spans and asserts both the retained newest entries and evicted oldest entries, leaving the task’s required eviction behavior unverified and allowing wrong-span deletion to ship.

[P1, confidence 100] src/sentry/scripts/spans/add-buffer.lua:62 — `if span_count > 1000 then` replaces the existing configurable `max_segment_spans` enforcement with a hard-coded limit, so any caller that configures a lower maximum silently retains up to 1,000 spans instead of its configured bound.

[P1, confidence 100] src/sentry/api/endpoints/organization_auditlogs.py:79 — `paginator_cls=OptimizedCursorPaginator,` selects a paginator whose new `math.floor(value)` key conversion receives `AuditLogEntry.datetime`, so every authorized optimized audit-log request containing a row raises `TypeError` instead of returning a page.

[P1, confidence 100] src/sentry/api/endpoints/organization_auditlogs.py:79 — `paginator_cls=OptimizedCursorPaginator,` adds a privileged audit-log pagination feature, so this change modifies an unrelated public endpoint instead of only optimizing spans-buffer insertion with eviction.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [P1, confidence 100] src/sentry/spans/buffer.py:197 — `p.zadd(set_key, {span.payload: span.end_timestamp_precise for span in subsegment})` — This changes live `span-buf:s:*` keys from Redis sets to sorted sets without a versioned keyspace or migration, so every pre-deploy buffered segment makes the new writer fail with WRONGTYPE and stops span ingestion until that key expires.

adjudication.rationale: The diff clearly shows a change from Redis SET commands (sadd, scard, sscan, sunionstore) to SORTED SET commands (zadd, zcard, zscan, zunionstore) for the same key pattern 'span-buf:s:{project_and_trace}:*'. In buffer.py line 197, the code changes from p.sadd() to p.zadd(). In add-buffer.lua, the commands change from scard/sunionstore to zcard/zunionstore. If there are existing keys in Redis that were created as SETs before this deployment, the new code attempting SORTED SET operations on them will fail with WRONGTYPE error. There's no migration strategy or key versioning visible in the diff to handle this transition, which would cause span ingestion failures during deployment until old keys expire.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [P2, confidence 100] src/sentry/scripts/spans/add-buffer.lua:30 — `for i = 0, 1000 do` — A trace whose redirect chain exceeds 1,001 links stops resolution at an intermediate span instead of the segment root, splitting one trace across independently flushed segments after this change reduced the previously documented 10,000-link bound.

adjudication.rationale: The diff clearly shows the loop limit being reduced from 10000 to 1000 in add-buffer.lua line 30. The original comment stated 'theoretically this limit means that segment trees of depth 10k may not be joined together correctly.' By reducing this to 1000, traces with redirect chains between 1001-10000 links that previously would have been resolved correctly will now stop at an intermediate span, causing trace segments to be split incorrectly. This is a real behavioral change that could cause data integrity issues for deep trace hierarchies.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [P2, confidence 75] src/sentry/scripts/spans/add-buffer.lua:47 — `span_count = redis.call("zunionstore", set_key, 2, set_key, span_key)` — The default ZUNIONSTORE SUM aggregation doubles the score of an identical payload present in both merged buffers, so eviction ranks that duplicate as newer than its real end timestamp and removes a newer distinct span when the segment crosses 1,000 members.

adjudication.rationale: The finding correctly identifies that ZUNIONSTORE with default SUM aggregation will add scores when the same payload exists in both sets being merged. Looking at the diff, spans are stored with their end_timestamp_precise as the score (line 196-198 in buffer.py). If the same span payload appears in both set_key and span_key (or parent_key), ZUNIONSTORE SUM will add the scores together, effectively doubling the timestamp. Later, zpopmin (line 55) removes spans with the lowest scores first. A span with an artificially doubled score would appear 'newer' than it actually is, potentially causing newer distinct spans to be evicted instead when the 1000 span limit is reached. This is a real correctness bug - the code should use AGGREGATE MIN or MAX to preserve the actual timestamp.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [P1, confidence 100] src/sentry/scripts/spans/add-buffer.lua:63 — `redis.call("zpopmin", set_key, span_count - 1000)` has no test that creates more than 1,000 timestamp-distinct spans and asserts both the retained newest entries and evicted oldest entries, leaving the task’s required eviction behavior unverified and allowing wrong-span deletion to ship.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds new eviction logic in add-buffer.lua (lines 55-58) that uses zpopmin to remove oldest spans when count exceeds 1000. This is new functionality that should be tested. Looking at the test files in the diff (test_buffer.py, test_flusher.py, test_consumer.py), none of them create more than a handful of spans - they all use small sets of 4-6 spans. The finding correctly identifies that there's no test verifying the eviction behavior works correctly (keeping newest 1000, removing oldest). This is a legitimate missing test for newly added nontrivial logic.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [P1, confidence 100] src/sentry/scripts/spans/add-buffer.lua:62 — `if span_count > 1000 then` replaces the existing configurable `max_segment_spans` enforcement with a hard-coded limit, so any caller that configures a lower maximum silently retains up to 1,000 spans instead of its configured bound.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows that in add-buffer.lua, a hard-coded limit of 1000 spans is enforced at line 62 (`if span_count > 1000 then redis.call('zpopmin', set_key, span_count - 1000)`). Meanwhile, in buffer.py, the code that previously enforced `max_segment_spans` (lines 446-452 in the old code checking `if len(payloads[key]) > self.max_segment_spans`) has been removed. This means the configurable `max_segment_spans` parameter is no longer being enforced - instead, a hard-coded 1000 limit in Lua takes over. If a caller configured a lower `max_segment_spans` value (e.g., 500), the system would now retain up to 1000 spans instead of respecting the configured bound.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [P1, confidence 100] src/sentry/api/endpoints/organization_auditlogs.py:79 — `paginator_cls=OptimizedCursorPaginator,` selects a paginator whose new `math.floor(value)` key conversion receives `AuditLogEntry.datetime`, so every authorized optimized audit-log request containing a row raises `TypeError` instead of returning a page.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_item_key() uses math.floor(value) or math.ceil(value) on the result of getattr(item, self.key). For audit logs, the order_by is '-datetime', so self.key would be 'datetime'. AuditLogEntry.datetime is a datetime object, and math.floor/math.ceil cannot operate on datetime objects - they require numeric types. This would raise a TypeError when trying to paginate audit log entries with the optimized paginator.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [P1, confidence 100] src/sentry/api/paginator.py:840 — `return int(math.floor(value) if self._is_asc(for_prev) else math.ceil(value))` — An authorized `optimized_pagination=true` audit-log request with at least one row passes its `datetime` sort value to `math.ceil`, raises TypeError, and returns a raw 500 instead of the endpoint's paginated response.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_item_key() at line 840 calls math.floor/math.ceil on `value = getattr(item, self.key)`. When used with the audit log endpoint (order_by='-datetime'), the key would be 'datetime' and the value would be a datetime object, not a number. math.ceil/math.floor cannot operate on datetime objects and will raise TypeError. The DateTimePaginator that was previously used has proper handling for datetime values, but this new OptimizedCursorPaginator does not. This is a real bug that would cause 500 errors when optimized_pagination=true is used.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [P2, confidence 100] src/sentry/scripts/spans/add-buffer.lua:30 — `for i = 0, 1000 do` — A trace whose parent chain exceeds 1,000 spans stops redirect resolution early, silently emits descendants under a different segment instead of the requested complete trace segment, and commits the corrupted result as success.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows the loop limit was reduced from 10000 to 1000 at line 30. The original code had a comment explaining 'theoretically this limit means that segment trees of depth 10k may not be joined together correctly.' By reducing this to 1000, traces with parent chains exceeding 1000 spans will now stop redirect resolution early. When the loop exits early without finding the final redirect target, the code continues to use whatever partial `set_span_id` was found, potentially causing spans to be grouped under incorrect segments. This is a real correctness bug - the change makes the system more likely to produce corrupted trace data for deep traces.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [P2, confidence 75] src/sentry/scripts/spans/add-buffer.lua:53 — `span_count = redis.call("zunionstore", set_key, 2, set_key, parent_key)` — A replayed span present in both merged sorted sets has its timestamp score summed by ZUNIONSTORE, so `zpopmin` retains that stale replay and silently evicts newer spans when the 1,000-span cap is enforced.

adjudication.rationale: The finding correctly identifies that ZUNIONSTORE with default AGGREGATE SUM behavior will sum scores when the same member exists in both sets. Looking at the diff, spans are stored with `span.end_timestamp_precise` as the score. If a span payload exists in both `set_key` and `parent_key` (e.g., due to replay or duplicate processing), ZUNIONSTORE will sum their timestamps, resulting in an incorrect score. When `zpopmin` is called to enforce the 1000-span limit, it removes spans with the lowest scores - but a replayed span with a doubled/summed timestamp would have an artificially high score and be retained, while legitimate newer spans with correct timestamps could be evicted. This is a real correctness bug in the span deduplication/merging logic.
